analysis:
Only docs/reference/protocol-messages.md changed (head lines 578 and 580-586). The change clarifies that `performance_measurements` sample_age_ms is measured since the newest observation, even if an older completed observation arrives later. It also says the Swift producer (EnginePerformanceMeasurements.observe) applies the same age rule independently to each workload bucket and current-posture series, with the existing receipt-order EWMA and sample counts retained. The patch says wire fields are unchanged. No code, auth, crypto, or trust-boundary behavior changes in the supplied evidence.

The rest of the supplied document (App Attest resume at lines 47-109, provider drain at 111-170, register and heartbeat tables) is unchanged context. It is consistent with TB-002, TB-011, T-053 and T-041. The resume text says the exchange grants no local trust, does not extend proof lifetime, and is bound to one socket with a fresh nonce and a 4 KiB bounded decode. The telemetry text calls prefix-cache and paged-storage telemetry observational, not routing inputs. Nothing in the diff weakens these statements.

Security relevance of the diff: sample_age_ms is untrusted provider-reported performance telemetry. The doc does not claim it gates authorization or routing trust, and the profile reference carries no self-certified curve. The Swift implementation file EnginePerformanceMeasurements.swift is not in the supplied evidence, so the described age semantics are not verified against code. This is a documentation claim only. No finding is supported. A reviewer of the Swift change should confirm that this timing logic does not enable stale or manipulated observations to affect coordinator scheduling beyond the existing clamps.
